name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Weber's large financial advantage ($922k vs. Bartie's negative cash)
Incumbent Weber running with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
model.rationale: This R+12 district with an entrenched incumbent leaves challenger Thurman Bartie with almost no path: he has raised only $27k and is in the red on cash, while Weber holds over $900k and faces no outside opposition. Markets price a Democratic win at roughly 4%, consistent with a Safe R call.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside-spending surge or a dramatic statewide Texas shift could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this Gulf Coast district, which leans Republican by about twelve points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position: roughly $920,000 on hand after raising nearly $1 million, plus modest outside support. Challenger Thurman Bartie has raised about $27,000 and reports negative cash on hand, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Weber about a 95% chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap makes this a Safe Republican seat, with the only real question being the size of Weber's winning margin.
